From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 Jun 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment posted but not applied: TeleGrid remittance 06/01

Laura / Marcus — looping you both in.

Summary: TeleGrid sent a remittance for 06/01 (attached) but our system mapped the receipt to the EU Non-VAT entity instead of the UK VAT-registered entity. That left the AR invoices still showing as open and created an unapplied credit in the non-VAT ledger.

Ask: can Marcus validate which journal entries we'd need to move the cash/receipt from entity A (EU Non-VAT) to entity B (UK VAT) and whether this needs a reversing/offset journal in revenue recognition for May? We’d like to get a clean AR aging and ensure revenue recognition mapping is intact.

I started a small triage workbook (attached) with the invoice numbers referenced by TeleGrid and a sketch of what I think the ledger correction should be — please update. Also cc: external contact so TeleGrid knows we have the thread open.

Attachments: VAT_reconciliation_workbook_Q2_2028.xlsx

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
(attachment: VAT_reconciliation_workbook_Q2_2028.xlsx - 120KB workbook stub)

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 5 Jun 2028 14:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Payment posted but not applied: TeleGrid remittance 06/01

Thanks Priya — reviewed the remittance and the workbook. Notes:  

- Root cause: Payment was ingested by our bank feed with counterparty tag mapping to EU-NONVAT entity due to an old remittance reference string (TeleGrid-INV- prefix) that maps to a shared customer record.
- Impact: Cash hit the wrong bank ledger (EU Non-VAT). AR invoices on UK VAT entity remain open. That created a temporary unapplied receipt in EU ledger of 82,540.00 EUR and left revenue recognition unchanged for May (no revenue reversal needed unless customer asks).

Proposed corrective entries (high-level):
1) Reverse unapplied receipt in EU ledger: DR Unapplied Cash 82,540.00 EUR / CR Bank Clearing 82,540.00 EUR (to clear the misapplied cash).
2) Post inter-entity cash movement: DR Bank Clearing EU 82,540.00 EUR / CR Bank Clearing UK 82,540.00 EUR (internal move).
3) Apply cash to AR in UK entity: DR Bank UK 82,540.00 EUR / CR Accounts Receivable 82,540.00 EUR (clears invoices).

If we need a revenue recognition adjustment I will flag it, but from the invoice-level check the revenue was recognized correctly in May for the underlying invoices — this is just a cash application mapping issue.

Action items: Laura, can you approve the journal entry set and confirm who will post (Treasury vs GL ops)? I can prepare reversing entries in the sub-ledger for audit trace.

—Marcus
Marcus Lin
Manager, General Ledger
Redwood Inference

Sven / TeleGrid finance — quick update from Redwood:  

Thank you for flagging this. We have identified the root cause (old remittance reference mapping to EU non-VAT entity) and approved the corrective journal set. GL Ops will post the reversing unapplied cash and inter-entity movement today, and Revenue Accounting will apply the cash to the UK VAT invoices once the bank clearing codes are reflected.

Expected timeline: entries posted by 2028-06-07 EOD PT; cash applied to invoices and AR aging updated by 2028-06-08. I’ve attached the reconciliation workbook we used for audit trace.

Next steps for TeleGrid: please ask your treasury team to include the invoice-level reference (INV#) in future remittances to avoid shared-customer mapping. That will let our bank feed route the payment directly to the UK VAT entity.

If you’d like, we can schedule a 30-minute cadence with your treasury to walk through the remittance formatting — happy to set that up.

Thanks,
Priya Natarajan
Senior Manager, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference
